headline: BEANS LEAD; SAUDI PIPELINE CRISIS KEEPS CRUDE BID
lead: Soybeans added 6¾ cents to $13.29 on strong demand and meal follow-through, while corn flatlined at $5.37 and cattle corrected across the board. WTI held $103.73 -- the Saudi pipeline shutdown, which began forcing spot crude sales outside the Strait of Hormuz last week, kept the bid alive despite a $1 pullback.
teaser: Beans firm at $13.29; Saudi pipeline crisis keeps crude bid despite session pullback.

one_number.context: Down from 7 the prior day, that number tells you the Hormuz premium in crude is not deflating; it is rebuilding. Diesel costs for fall fieldwork stay elevated.

yesterdays_call.note: Feeders fell to $340.05 today, well under $345; the supply-tightness bid is fading as the Aug 24 Douglas reopening approaches.
yesterdays_call.call_line: Called feeder cattle up toward $345.0 ($343.7 when the call was made). It closed at $340.05.

action: New-crop beans at a 52-week high: price the first 10% on any settle above $13.35. Do not wait.

sections.title: BEANS FIRM; CORN FLAT
sections.body:
- Soybeans closed at **$13.29**, up 6¾ cents, with AgWeb citing strong demand and meal follow-through as the twin engines; soybean oil added 0.6% alongside.
- Corn settled at $5.37, off a quarter-cent, effectively unchanged; no fund flow, no weather headline, no reason to move.
sections.so_what: Beans are doing the work on their own; corn is along for the ride.

sections.title: CRUDE HOLDS; CATTLE CORRECT
sections.body: - WTI eased to $103.73, off about $1, but the Saudi pipeline shutdown forcing spot sales outside Hormuz is the reason crude is at $103 in the first place, not a reason to sell it.
sections.so_what: Crude's bid is structural; cattle's correction is a pause, not a breakdown.

outside_the_pit.title: Farm Groups Push Back Hard on 24-Hour Commodity Trading
outside_the_pit.body: Grain elevators and farm organizations are fighting proposals to move futures markets to round-the-clock trading, arguing it raises hedging costs and complexity for producers who cannot monitor screens overnight.

watch_list.desc: Weekly export sales: beans above 400K MT confirms demand is real, not position-squaring.
Hormuz tanker count: below 5 vessels/day keeps crude above $102 and fall diesel costs elevated.
Douglas AZ port reopening for Mexican feeders: feeder close below $338 signals the market is pricing returning supply.

daily_quote.text: Obstacles are those frightful things you see when you take your eyes off your goal.

source_summary: CME locked closes; AgWeb; oilprice.com; beefmagazine.com; thefencepost.com; Reuters ship-tracking via oilprice.com
